items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: he was a mainstay in my band for years. I got Mickey. We call him Mickey. Mickey Alcorn.

ctx.x: Anything, let's see, Alvin Alcorn, of course, was over here for a while, I understand, and played with you. He was interviewed for Tulane, too, but I've never heard his interview. Another fellow up there, Dick Allen, interviewed him.

Well, yes, he was a mainstay in my band for years. I got Mickey. We call him Mickey. Mickey Alcorn. I brought him out of New Orleans when he was a kid, too. I never heard him call that Mickey. Mickey. I never heard him. Just when you see him, say, hi, Mickey. Yeah. I never heard anybody call him that over there.
He still plays the parade. Oh, he's fine.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: We had the James sisters and Mickey and I would do a little scene. He would sit on my lap and I would finger his arm.

ctx.x: When you were working on the percentage, you would watch the game.

Well, now there you go again. A lot of times they asked me why did I stop playing like I did. Well, for more reasons than one. That was one of them to stay on the door and watch the proceedings there and make sure that I got everything was mine. That's what happened when we were on the verge of being lynched in Thomasville, Georgia, playing a percentage dance and the school teacher had charge of the dance. And naturally I was up there checking the door with him when the policemen came in to arrest everybody,…

We have talked about it some, but I didn't get everything down, you know. Oh, we didn't? Yeah. Like that, you know, and every time you tell something you get more. Did you ever know a fella named Floyd Snellson?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I said everybody in the band had nicknames.

ctx.x: Who just called him Mickey? Just came out.

Right. Yeah. Now, maybe he might remember why, but I don't know, but I remember this. Everyone, like I was talking to someone last night, oh, Cottrell was here last night, and Miss Simmons, my school teacher, was asking me why I continued to call him Bucks. Well, I said I called him Bucks, and I called him Riney, I said everybody in the band had nicknames. Even me, I was called the old man. I was 21 years old, but I was called the old man.
But, what was the Bucks having to do with it?
